meta.title: Geography of Middle-earth — Rohan, Gondor, Moria, Lothlórien
meta.description: Overview of the places of Middle-earth by region: Rohan and surroundings, Misty Mountains and Moria, forests and elven realms, fortresses, north-west, Mordor, south and east.

hero.subtitle: A map by region — from Eriador to Mordor.

intro: This page summarises the main places of Middle-earth as Tolkien describes them. We structure them by region so you can find your bearings even without a map. For every place you'll find a short description, its role in the War of the Ring and a possible link to a game army.
alert_map: A map is not yet part of this overview. We plan to add it as a separate interactive layer where you'll be able to filter by people, age and side of the conflict.
lang_notice: Descriptions of individual places are currently translated; some terminology may be refined in future updates.

places.name: Rohan / Riddermark / the Mark
places.desc: The land of the horse-lords, lying between the White Mountains and the rivers Anduin and Isen. It was settled in later ages by Eorl's people in return for aiding Gondor. For hundreds of years the Rohirrim have kept their horses, their spears and their oath to Gondor.

places.name: Calenardhon
places.desc: The old name for the same land in the days when it belonged to Gondor. After Eorl's coming Calenardhon became Rohan.

places.name: Gap of Rohan
places.desc: The wide passage between the White Mountains and the Misty Mountains. A gateway between Eriador and the south; a key strategic point.

places.name: Fords of Isen
places.desc: Shallows by which the river is crossed from Rohan into Eriador. A site of repeated battles — Saruman struck at Rohan here before Helm's Deep would decide the war.

places.name: Edoras and Meduseld
places.desc: The capital of Rohan on a hill in the eastern part of the land. At its head stands the golden hall **Meduseld** — the king's seat.

places.name: Helm's Deep / the Hornburg
places.desc: A fortress in a corner of the White Mountains. A refuge for the people of Rohan against an enemy who cannot win an open battle. The place where Saruman's defeat was sealed.

regions.h2: The Misty Mountains and the deeps below

places.name: Misty Mountains
places.desc: A long range running through Middle-earth from north to south. The chief barrier between Eriador and Rhovanion. In their depths dwell orcs, dragons and an old darkness.

places.name: Khazad-dûm / Moria
places.desc: An ancient dwarven realm hewn into the depths of the mountains. Abandoned after the awakening of the Balrog and the fall of King Durin. Centuries later Balin's attempted return ended with the slaughter of his whole company. For the Fellowship of the Ring it was a road none of them wished to take.

places.name: Caradhras (the Cruel)
places.desc: A high peak of the Misty Mountains whose pass the Fellowship was forced to abandon — Caradhras itself stood against them.

places.name: Fangorn
places.desc: An ancient forest at the eastern feet of the Misty Mountains. The home of the Ents, who long slumber there. The meeting of Merry and Pippin with Treebeard rouses their whole Entmoot — and in the end brings down Isengard.

places.name: Lothlórien (the Golden Wood)
places.desc: The realm of Galadriel and Celeborn — protected by Nenya, one of the Three Elven Rings. Heart of the mallorn-trees with their gleaming gold leaves. For the Fellowship a place of rest and of gifts that would later prove vital.

places.name: Caras Galadhon
places.desc: The chief city of Lothlórien — a city in the trees, built around the tallest mallorns. The seat of Galadriel and Celeborn.

places.name: Mirkwood
places.desc: Once called Greenwood the Great, later darkened by the shadow of Dol Guldur. The home of Thranduil and the Wood-elves. After the destruction of the One Ring its light returns.

places.name: Imladris (Rivendell)
places.desc: A hidden elven realm in north-western Middle-earth, the seat of Elrond. The site of the Council at which the Fellowship of the Ring was formed.

places.name: The Grey Havens (Mithlond)
places.desc: The haven at the mouth of the river Lhûn, the seat of Círdan the Shipwright. From here the elves sail westward over the Sea. At the end of the tale Frodo, Bilbo and the bearers of the Three Rings depart this way.

places.name: Isengard / Angrenost / Orthanc
places.desc: A vale at the southern foot of the Misty Mountains. At its centre stands the black tower of **Orthanc** from elder days. Saruman's seat, and later his forge in which the Uruk-hai are bred. The fall of Isengard came when the Ents broke its dams and Saruman was left a prisoner in Orthanc.

places.name: Minas Tirith
places.desc: The capital of Gondor — the Tower of Guard beneath the White Mountain Mindolluin. Seven concentric levels carved into the slope, divided by walls.

places.name: Osgiliath
places.desc: The old capital of Gondor, now largely a ruin. A strategic bridge across the Anduin — whoever holds Osgiliath holds the way to Minas Tirith.

places.name: Dol Amroth
places.desc: A coastal princedom in southern Gondor. The seat of Prince Imrahil, of a line whose blood still keeps the memory of an elven kinship.

places.name: Dol Guldur
places.desc: A fortress in the south of Mirkwood. For long centuries it was held by a shadow, until its master revealed himself as Sauron returned. After the War of the Ring Galadriel casts it down.

places.name: Erebor
places.desc: The Lonely Mountain in eastern Rhovanion. An ancient dwarven kingdom. Restored after the fall of the dragon Smaug, it joins the Battle of Dale during the War of the Ring.

places.name: Eriador
places.desc: A wide land between the Misty Mountains and the Blue Mountains. Once the heart of the Northern Kingdom of Arnor; today almost empty save for the Shire, Bree and a few other remnants.

places.name: Arnor
places.desc: The northern kingdom of Men. Over the centuries it broke apart in fratricidal strife and was finally destroyed by Angmar. Its descendants now wander as the Rangers of the North.

places.name: The Shire
places.desc: The land of the hobbits. A quiet, fertile, well-tended corner of north-western Middle-earth. The Rangers have long guarded it from afar without the hobbits ever knowing.

places.name: Bree
places.desc: A town of Men and hobbits at the crossing of the East Road and the old North Road. The Prancing Pony — the inn where many fates begin to entwine.

places.name: Mordor — the Black Land
places.desc: The seat of Sauron. Hemmed in by the Ephel Dúath in the west and the Ered Lithui in the north. Within lie Gorgoroth (fire and ash) and Núrn (the slave-fields that feed Sauron's armies).

places.name: Mount Doom (Orodruin)
places.desc: The volcano in which Sauron forged the One Ring. The only place where the Ring can be unmade.

places.name: Barad-dûr
places.desc: Sauron's Dark Tower. It stands as long as the One Ring endures. With its destruction the tower falls.

places.name: Cirith Ungol and the Black Gate
places.desc: **Cirith Ungol** — the pass with Shelob and the watchtower beyond it. **The Morannon (the Black Gate)** — the chief entrance to Mordor from the north, the place of the final battle.

places.name: Minas Morgul
places.desc: Once the Gondorian tower of Minas Ithil, later seized by the Nazgûl. The seat of the Witch-king, until he rides forth to the Pelennor Fields.

places.name: Harad
places.desc: A wide belt of warm lands south of Gondor. Divided into Near and Far Harad. Tribes of the Haradrim and the great beasts called mûmakil.

places.name: Umbar
places.desc: The great southern haven. After the fall of Númenor it became the seat of the Black Númenóreans, and in the Third Age a Corsair stronghold threatening the coasts of Gondor.

places.name: Rhûn
places.desc: Vast plains east of Mordor. Home of the Easterlings — diverse tribes who in the familiar tale most often serve Sauron.

footnote: Texts are paraphrased, without direct quotations from Tolkien's books.
